race: Formula 1 TAG Heuer Gran Premio de España 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, because Madrid is here for the first time, and the new circuit is trying to be our friend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Organisers are making changes after criticism of the inaugural race, and honestly, that is the best kind of news for a young street that wants to grow.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: A fresh layout can be exciting, but it needs to feel fair before the lights go out, and the fans deserve a clean, competitive run.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Norris is calling himself insanely unlucky after a virtual safety car cost him what looked like a certain win at the Spanish Grand Prix.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: One timing decision can turn a victory lap into a podium hug, and Formula One should rethink that kind of late race luck, especially when the lead is already in your pocket.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Honda also changed its Formula One design boss after a slow start to its return, which is a big behind the scenes shake up for the grid, and the teams will be watching closely.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the kind of move that can change a whole season, even if we do not see it in the standings right away, and maybe not until the back half.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Driver ratings keep calling Antonelli impressive, and the big question is whether he is generational talent or just a hot hand when the stakes rise.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That question is exactly why Mercedes will be the team to watch when the weekend gets loud and the pressure builds on a street that can be unforgiving.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: We are pre practice, so no free practice data yet, just season form, fresh news and this circuit's history, and a lot of good vibes.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: My top one is Kimi Antonelli, because seven wins and the championship lead are hard to ignore this close to any of us.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: How do you beat a driver who keeps finding pace when the race gets serious and the track is still new for everyone else?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: You do not, you just hope Madrid behaves when the pressure is on, the gaps are tiny, and the barriers are close and the cars are all fighting for position.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: My second is George Russell, because he is the strong second Mercedes driver with a good street circuit record and a calm left foot.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: A street circuit is his kind of puzzle, and Mercedes should love the tight rhythm of this place all weekend, from lights to chequered flag.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But I am keeping Lewis Hamilton in third, not out of respect, but because the man knows this place cold from the first lap.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Consistent podiums and excellent historical circuit form are hard to argue with in a brand new venue, especially when the car is strong.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I am not buying it, because Ferrari has to match Mercedes on a street that is still proving itself under full race pressure.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Easy to say now, until Hamilton puts on a masterclass and makes everyone else look a little slow in front of the camera.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Leclerc is strong recently, but the circuit edge is thinner than I need for a confident top three pick when Mercedes is this hot.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Verstappen has the ceiling, but the recent inconsistency keeps him just outside my top five for Madrid on a layout that punishes small mistakes.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Piastri has won here before, so do not sleep on McLaren's second car when the race gets chaotic and the track is still changing.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time, our low confidence gamble is Arvid Lindblad in tenth, and yes, it is a real gamble, but the upside is fun.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Consistent top ten form is there, but a practice crash flags Madrid risk, and this layout can be unforgiving when the barriers are close.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lawson is points rich and consistent, while Gasly can always find points, even if street racing is weaker for Gasly in particular.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: If Lindblad avoids the barriers, Racing Bulls could be the weekend surprise that nobody priced in, and the room will love it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is the full top ten, Kimi Antonelli, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Lando Norris, Charles Leclerc, Max Verstappen, Oscar Piastri, Liam Lawson, Pierre Gasly, Arvid Lindblad. Madrid, Madrid, let us see who takes the wheel this weekend, and we will be right here.
